About the Instructor
Dr. Matthias König is a researcher and educator at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, where he leads the Systems Medicine of the Liver group. His work focuses on computational modeling, pharmacokinetics, and digital health education. He is passionate about making complex biomedical processes understandable and accessible through open, interactive learning resources.
This course was developed as part of the BUA Open Science Ambassador program to promote Open Science at the Berlin Universities.

title: uv
text:
What is uv?
Interactive introduction to fast Python environment & package management with uv
uv is a next-generation Python package manager and virtual environment tool developed by Astral (creators of Ruff). It aims to replace slow and fragmented Python tooling with a single, fast, unified solution.
At a glance, uv is:
uv removes a large part of Python’s traditional environment chaos and speeds up everything dramatically.

title: uv
text:
⚡ Extremely fast — built in Rust, 10–100× faster than pip/conda/poetry
🧱 A unified tool — environments, dependency resolution, package management, execution — all in one
📦 Fully compatible with the Python ecosystem — pyproject.toml, PEP standards, pip-compatible commands
🛠 Drop-in replacement for many tools — pip, virtualenv, pipx, dependency solvers, executors
🛡 Reliable & reproducible — lockfiles ensure deterministic builds
🧰 Simple — no environment activation needed for most tasks

title: uv
text:
🔧 Installation
macOS / Linux:
curl -fsSL https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Windows (PowerShell):
irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex

✏️ Notes

Where was uv installed? (~/.local/bin or system PATH)
Did the script detect your Python version?

title: uv
text:
🔍 List installed packages
uv pip list

title: uv
text:
🔍 Show the dependency tree
uv tree

❓ Explore

Which packages are direct dependencies?
Which ones are transitive?
Is the tree readable?

title: uv
section: 📌 A — Add a new package (example: rich)
text:
📌 A — Add a new package (example: rich)
uv add rich
Check:
uv pip list
uv tree

title: uv
text:
📌 B — Remove the package
uv remove rich
Then verify:
uv pip list
uv tree

title: uv
text:
📌 C — Add it again (cached!)
uv add rich
Check the environment again:
uv pip list
uv tree

❓ Observations

Was the second installation faster? Why?
Did the lockfile and pyproject update correctly?

Our Pledge
We as members, contributors, students and teachers pledge to make participation in our course and community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.
We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Our Standards
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our course and community include:

Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
Public or private harassment
Publishing others’ private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Enforcement Responsibilities
Teachers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.
Teachers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Scope
This Code of Conduct applies within all learning and community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official email address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Enforcement
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at konigmatt@googlemail.com. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.
All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

title: Open Science Workshop
text:
Introduction & Motivation
Reproducibility is a cornerstone of modern computational research — yet many everyday workflows in data science, systems biology, and computational modeling remain fragile, siloed, or dependent on personal conventions. Researchers frequently encounter challenges such as:

inconsistent Python environments
missing metadata or unclear provenance
scattered reference collections
non-reproducible documents or analysis pipelines
difficulty sharing results in open and citable formats

This workshop addresses these challenges by providing a practical, hands-on introduction to tools that make computational research open, transparent, and verifiably reproducible.
The workshop is made possible through support from the Open Science Ambassador Program at the Berlin University Alliance (BUA), which aims to empower researchers to adopt open, FAIR, and reproducible practices across all phases of the research lifecycle.

title: Open Science Workshop
text:
🎯 Workshop Goals
By the end of the day, participants will:

understand core principles of open science and reproducible workflows
learn to manage Python environments reliably using uv
create citable research assets using Zenodo
organize and maintain structured reference libraries with Zotero
produce professional, reproducible documents using Typst
publish integrated analyses and reports using Quarto
reflect on their own workflow practices through LEGO® Serious Play
gain confidence to integrate open tools into their daily research

title: Open Science Workshop
text:
🧰 Tools Covered in the Course






TipTip: Customize Your Learning Path



The course does not have to be done linearly—you can explore the content in any order. Choose the learning path that best suits your goals, interests, or current knowledge level. This way, you stay engaged and make the most of your learning experience.



uv — Reliable Python Environment Management (?sec-uv) A fast, modern tool for Python environments and package management, enabling reproducible computational modelling across machines and teams.
Zenodo — Citable Research Outputs (?sec-zenodo) A platform for sharing datasets, code, models, and workflows with persistent DOIs. Essential for transparency, credit, and long-term accessibility.
Zotero — Reference & Knowledge Management (?sec-zotero) Open-source reference management for organizing literature, annotations, and citations across projects.
Typst — Modern Document Preparation (?sec-typst) A next-generation typesetting system designed for scientific writing: fast, reproducible, expressive, and accessible.
Quarto — Reproducible Publishing (?sec-quarto) A unified toolchain for scientific and technical publishing, enabling dynamic reports, manuscripts, slides, and websites.
